title: Jeremiah Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 5.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem
I will get me unto the great men
Wherefore a lion out of the forest shall slay them
How shall I pardon thee for this?
questions.correctAnswer: Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: This is the first command given in the chapter, as stated in Jeremiah 5:1.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about those who swear falsely?
questions.explanation: The verse states that they say, 'The LORD liveth; surely they swear falsely.' This is found in Jeremiah 5:2.

questions.question: What have the people made their faces harder than?
questions.explanation: The text states they have made their faces harder than a rock, as found in Jeremiah 5:3.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about the people in Jeremiah 5:4?
questions.explanation: The verse describes the people as poor and foolish because they do not know the way of the LORD, as seen in Jeremiah 5:4.

questions.question: What have the great men of the people known according to Jeremiah 5:5?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that the great men have known the way of the LORD and the judgment of their God, as stated in Jeremiah 5:5.

questions.question: What creatures are mentioned as threats to the people in Jeremiah 5:6?
questions.explanation: The verse lists these creatures as threats due to the people's transgressions, as found in Jeremiah 5:6.

questions.question: What have the children of the people done according to Jeremiah 5:7?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the children have forsaken the LORD and sworn by false gods, as seen in Jeremiah 5:7.

questions.question: How does the LORD describe the people in Jeremiah 5:8?
questions.explanation: The text describes them as fed horses in the morning, indicating their eagerness after their neighbors' wives, as found in Jeremiah 5:8.

questions.question: What does the LORD declare He will do concerning their sins in Jeremiah 5:9?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD will visit for these things and avenge His soul on such a nation, as found in Jeremiah 5:9.

questions.question: What instruction does the LORD give in Jeremiah 5:10?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs to destroy and take away her battlements, as they are not the LORD's, as stated in Jeremiah 5:10.

questions.question: Who has dealt very treacherously against the LORD according to Jeremiah 5:11?
options: The house of Israel and the house of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Israel and the house of Judah
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that both the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt treacherously against the LORD, as found in Jeremiah 5:11.

questions.question: Is it true that the children of the people have sworn by false gods?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the children have sworn by them that are no gods, confirming this is true as stated in Jeremiah 5:7.

questions.question: Is it true that the people have refused to receive correction?
questions.explanation: The text indicates that they have refused to receive correction, as stated in Jeremiah 5:3.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD will not visit for their sins?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the LORD shall visit for these things, indicating that it is false to say He will not, as found in Jeremiah 5:9.

questions.question: Is it false that the people have always followed the way of the LORD?
questions.explanation: The text indicates that they do not know the way of the LORD, confirming it is false to say they have always followed it, as stated in Jeremiah 5:4.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 5:12, what did the people say about the LORD and the calamities that might come upon them?
options: It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine
The LORD will punish us for our sins
We will be delivered from all troubles
The prophets speak the truth and we must listen
questions.correctAnswer: It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:12 states that the people have belied the LORD and said, 'It is not he; neither shall evil come upon us; neither shall we see sword nor famine.'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 5:14 promise will happen if the people speak the words denying the LORD's power as in Jeremiah 5:13?
options: The LORD will make His words in their mouth fire that devours the people
The people will be immediately forgiven
The prophets will become more powerful
The people will be blessed with peace
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will make His words in their mouth fire that devours the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:14 says because they speak the words denying the LORD, He will make His words in their mouth fire, and the people wood that it shall devour them.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 5:15 describe the nation that the LORD will bring upon Israel?
options: A mighty and ancient nation whose language is not understood
A weak nation that will be easily defeated
A nation that will bring peace and prosperity
A nation that speaks the same language as Israel
questions.correctAnswer: A mighty and ancient nation whose language is not understood
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:15 describes the nation as mighty, ancient, and with a language the people do not know or understand.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 5:16 and 5:17 together describe the impact of the invading nation on Israel's resources?
options: They are mighty warriors who will consume the harvest, bread, flocks, herds, vines, and cities
They will peacefully coexist and share resources
They will only attack the cities but leave the harvest alone
They will be defeated before reaching Israel's resources
questions.correctAnswer: They are mighty warriors who will consume the harvest, bread, flocks, herds, vines, and cities
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:16-17 explains the invaders are mighty men with quivers like open graves, who will eat up the harvest, bread, flocks, herds, vines, fig trees, and impoverish the fenced cities.

questions.question: What is the significance of the LORD not making a full end with Israel as stated in Jeremiah 5:18?
options: It shows God's mercy despite Israel's disobedience
It means Israel will never be punished
It implies the punishment will be mild and temporary
It indicates the people will return to their sins quickly
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's mercy despite Israel's disobedience
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:18 states the LORD will not make a full end, indicating His mercy even though judgment is coming.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 5:19, what reason should Israel give when asked why the LORD is doing these things to them?
options: Because they forsook the LORD and served strange gods, so they will serve strangers in a foreign land
Because the LORD is angry without cause
Because the prophets have misled them
Because the land is cursed from birth
questions.correctAnswer: Because they forsook the LORD and served strange gods, so they will serve strangers in a foreign land
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:19 explains the LORD's actions are due to Israel forsaking Him and serving strange gods, resulting in serving strangers in a foreign land.

questions.question: Who is the message of Jeremiah 5:20-21 addressed to, and how are they described?
options: The house of Jacob, described as foolish and without understanding
The prophets, described as false and deceitful
The kings, described as wise and just
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Jacob, described as foolish and without understanding
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:20-21 calls on the house of Jacob and describes them as foolish people without understanding, who have eyes but see not and ears but hear not.

questions.question: What natural boundary does the LORD mention in Jeremiah 5:22 to illustrate His power and authority?
options: The sand set as the bound of the sea that it cannot pass
The stars fixed in the sky
The rivers flowing to the ocean
questions.correctAnswer: The sand set as the bound of the sea that it cannot pass
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:22 speaks of the LORD placing the sand as the boundary for the sea, which the waves cannot cross, showing His sovereign control.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 5:12-13 show the people's attitude toward the LORD's prophets and warnings?
options: They deny the LORD and say prophets are wind with no word in them
They eagerly listen and obey the prophets
They are confused but willing to learn
They honor the prophets as messengers of God
questions.correctAnswer: They deny the LORD and say prophets are wind with no word in them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:12-13 reveals the people belied the LORD and said the prophets are like wind with no word, rejecting their warnings.

questions.question: In the context of Jeremiah 5:14-15, what is the purpose of the LORD making His words fire in the people's mouths?
options: To bring judgment and consume the rebellious people like wood burnt by fire
To give the people power to prophesy rightly
To comfort the people in their distress
To teach the people how to pray
questions.correctAnswer: To bring judgment and consume the rebellious people like wood burnt by fire
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:14 promises that the LORD will make His words fire in their mouths, and the people wood, so the fire devours them, symbolizing judgment.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith and trust can be drawn from Jeremiah 5:21, where the people have eyes but see not and ears but hear not?
options: True faith requires not just seeing and hearing but understanding and obeying God's word
Seeing and hearing are enough to maintain faith
Faith depends only on emotions, not perception
questions.correctAnswer: True faith requires not just seeing and hearing but understanding and obeying God's word
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:21 highlights that mere physical senses without understanding lead to foolishness, teaching that faith involves comprehension and obedience.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 5:19 challenge believers to consider the consequences of forsaking God and serving other gods?
options: Forsaking God leads to serving strangers in a foreign land as a consequence
Forsaking God has no real consequences
Serving other gods will bring prosperity
God will immediately restore those who forsake Him
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking God leads to serving strangers in a foreign land as a consequence
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:19 explains that forsaking God and serving strange gods results in exile and serving strangers, emphasizing consequences of disobedience.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 5:22, what does the inability of the sea to pass its boundary symbolize about God's nature?
options: God's sovereign control and unchanging decrees
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign control and unchanging decrees
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:22 uses the sea's boundary to illustrate God's sovereign authority and the permanence of His decrees.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 5:18 states that the LORD will completely destroy the house of Israel without mercy.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:18 clearly states the LORD will not make a full end with Israel, showing He will not completely destroy them.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 5:12-13 indicates that the people fully trusted the LORD and His prophets.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:12-13 shows the people denied the LORD and said the prophets' words were wind, indicating distrust.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 5.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah say about the people's heart in Jeremiah 5:23?
questions.explanation: This answer is correct as Jeremiah 5:23 states, 'But this people hath a revolting and a rebellious heart; they are revolted and gone.'

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 5:25, what has turned away good things from the people?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is found in Jeremiah 5:25, which states, 'Your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withholden good things from you.'

questions.question: In Jeremiah 5:29, what does the LORD say He will do regarding the nation's actions?
options: He will visit for these things
questions.correctAnswer: He will visit for these things
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:29 states, 'Shall I not visit for these things? saith the LORD: shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this?'

questions.question: What do the houses of the wicked men contain according to Jeremiah 5:27?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:27 explains, 'As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit: therefore they are become great, and waxen rich.'

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 5:28 say about how the wicked judge?
options: They do not judge the cause of the fatherless
They seek justice for the needy
questions.correctAnswer: They do not judge the cause of the fatherless
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'They judge not the cause, the cause of the fatherless, yet they prosper; and the right of the needy do they not judge.' (Jeremiah 5:28)

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'revolting' in Jeremiah 5:23 mean?
questions.explanation: The word 'revolting' in Hebrew indicates a turning away from God, implying rebellion against divine authority.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Jeremiah 5:31 regarding the prophets and priests?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:31 employs parallelism, contrasting the actions of prophets and priests with the people's acceptance of their falsehoods.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment for wickedness seen in Jeremiah 5:29?
questions.explanation: Romans 2:6 states, 'Who will render to every man according to his deeds,' echoing the judgment theme seen in Jeremiah 5:29.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the warning against false prophets found in Jeremiah 5:31?
questions.explanation: Matthew 24:11 states, 'And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many,' fulfilling the warning against false prophets in Jeremiah 5:31.

questions.question: What comes before the statement about the people's heart in Jeremiah 5:23?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:22 precedes verse 23, where the LORD observes the people's lack of fear and deceitful behavior.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 5:26, what do the wicked men do?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:26 states, 'For among my people are found wicked men: they lay wait, as he that setteth snares; they set a trap, they catch men.'

questions.question: God is described as doing what in Jeremiah 5:30 regarding the nation?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:30 describes a 'wonderful and horrible thing' committed in the land, indicating God's impending judgment.

questions.question: The statement that 'the prophets prophesy falsely' in Jeremiah 5:31 is an example of which literary device?
questions.explanation: This statement is ironic because the prophets, who are supposed to speak truth, are instead speaking falsehoods, misleading the people.

questions.question: It is true that the people in Jeremiah 5:31 love the false prophecies?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:31 states, 'and my people love to have it so,' indicating their preference for false prophecies.

questions.question: The people of Judah are described as having a fear of the LORD in Jeremiah 5:24?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:24 indicates that they do not say in their heart, 'Let us now fear the LORD our God,' implying a lack of fear for God.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 5:1 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Human righteousness can atone for the sins of a whole city
God’s judgment is avoidable if even one just person is found
Divine pardon is granted regardless of human justice
All humanity is incapable of executing true judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is avoidable if even one just person is found
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:1 shows that if a man who executes judgment and seeks the truth is found, God will pardon the city, indicating that divine judgment can be averted through the presence of righteous individuals.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human apostasy is taught in Jeremiah 5:7?
options: God’s people remain faithful despite external influences
Fornication symbolizes Israel’s spiritual unfaithfulness to God
God’s blessings eliminate the possibility of idolatry
Children are not responsible for their spiritual state
questions.correctAnswer: Fornication symbolizes Israel’s spiritual unfaithfulness to God
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:7 uses the metaphor of adultery and assembling in harlots’ houses to depict Israel's spiritual infidelity by forsaking God and worshiping false gods.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine sovereignty and judgment is taught in Jeremiah 5:15?
options: God’s judgment is limited to familiar nations only
God raises unknown nations to execute His judgment
God’s judgment is always immediate and local
Foreign nations act independently of God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: God raises unknown nations to execute His judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:15 teaches that God will bring a mighty, ancient nation from afar whose language is unknown to Israel to execute judgment upon them, highlighting divine sovereignty over nations.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 5:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:22 demonstrates God's omnipotence by describing His control over natural boundaries like the sea, which cannot pass the limits He has set by a perpetual decree.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most emphasized in Jeremiah 5:18?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:18 expresses that despite Israel's sins, God will not make a full end with them, demonstrating His longsuffering and patience.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 5:10 prepare for the theme of divine judgment fulfilled in the book of Ezekiel?
options: It predicts the complete destruction of Jerusalem without exception
It commands partial destruction, preserving remnants for restoration
It denies any divine judgment on Jerusalem
It focuses on external enemies rather than internal sin
questions.correctAnswer: It commands partial destruction, preserving remnants for restoration
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:10 orders destruction but not a full end, which foreshadows Ezekiel's prophecies of judgment balanced with restoration for Israel.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 5:31 connect with the New Testament teaching on false prophets in Matthew 7?
options: Both affirm that false prophecy is accepted by the people
Both reject any role of prophets in the church
Both teach that all prophecy is divinely inspired
Both encourage unquestioning acceptance of religious leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Both affirm that false prophecy is accepted by the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:31 notes the false prophets and priests ruling by them, with the people loving it, which parallels Matthew 7’s warning about false prophets being accepted by many.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 5:23 and 5:25 teach about human rebellion and divine providence?
options: Human rebellion is inevitable but does not affect divine providence
Rebellion provokes God to withhold blessings and good things
God’s providence always overrides human sin without consequence
Human sin is insignificant in God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: Rebellion provokes God to withhold blessings and good things
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:23 and 5:25 together show that the people's rebellious hearts and iniquities cause God to withhold rain and good things, linking sin with divine discipline in providence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 5:26 and 5:28 teach about social injustice and divine judgment?
options: Wealth and prosperity are signs of divine blessing despite injustice
Social injustice corrupts society and provokes God’s judgment
Judging the needy is optional for godly leaders
Injustice is unrelated to covenant responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Social injustice corrupts society and provokes God’s judgment
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:26 and 5:28 describe wicked men trapping others and failing to judge the cause of the needy, highlighting social injustice that leads to divine judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 5:12 and 5:13 teach about false assurance and prophetic failure?
options: False assurances undermine faith and true prophecy
Denial of evil leads to spiritual prosperity
Prophetic words are always true regardless of content
questions.correctAnswer: False assurances undermine faith and true prophecy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:12-13 teach that Israel falsely claims evil will not come and that prophets become like wind with no word in them, showing false assurance and failed prophecy.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Jeremiah 5:14-17 teaches that God’s judgment is arbitrary and indiscriminate. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is a direct consequence of persistent sin and rebellion
God punishes innocent people along with the guilty without reason
Judgment is random and unrelated to the people's behavior
God’s words in the prophet’s mouth bring destruction regardless of context
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is a direct consequence of persistent sin and rebellion
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:14-17 shows that God’s words become fire to devour the people because of their persistent transgressions and backslidings, indicating just and purposeful judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Jeremiah 5:9 teach about divine justice and vengeance?
options: God’s soul is passive and does not seek vengeance
Divine justice includes the vindication of God’s honor
God forgives all offenses without exception
Human vengeance is identical to divine justice
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice includes the vindication of God’s honor
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:9 emphasizes that God’s soul will be avenged on such a nation, teaching that God’s justice involves vindicating His honor against rebellion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Jeremiah 5:29 highlight regarding God’s response to social injustice?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:29 states God’s soul will be avenged on the nation for their injustice, emphasizing His attribute of justice against wrongdoing.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Jeremiah 5:4 and 5:5 teach about knowledge of God and covenant responsibility?
options: All leaders faithfully uphold God’s covenant
Knowledge of God implies responsibility to remain under His yoke
Only the poor know the way of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Knowledge of God implies responsibility to remain under His yoke
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:4-5 contrast the poor who do not know God’s way with the great men who do but have broken His yoke, teaching that knowledge entails covenantal responsibility.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 5:21-24 develop the theme of spiritual blindness and covenant unfaithfulness?
options: The people see and understand God’s works perfectly
Despite having senses, the people fail to perceive God’s covenant blessings
Spiritual blindness is unrelated to covenant faithfulness
God punishes only those who physically cannot see or hear
questions.correctAnswer: Despite having senses, the people fail to perceive God’s covenant blessings
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:21-24 rebukes the people for having eyes and ears but not seeing or hearing, symbolizing spiritual blindness and failure to honor God’s covenant provision.
